adjudication_records.issue_text: Ember {{each}} helper uses 'itemView' option but the correct option is 'itemViewClass', causing members to render as empty elements and group-member view to be dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs`, members are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` (no block). The PR also adds a `group-member` view (`admin/views/group-member.js.es6`) and template (`admin/templates/group_member.hbs`) intended to be used as the per-item renderer. In Ember’s `{{each}}`/collection helper, the option for specifying the per-item view is typically `itemViewClass`, not `itemView`; if `itemView` is ignored, the loop has no block/template to render and would produce empty output, leaving the newly added view/template effectively unused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: {{#unless automatic}} in group_member.hbs checks 'automatic' on the member (user) context instead of the group, so remove link renders for automatic groups and clicking it produces a 422

adjudication.rationale: In the new `group_member.hbs` template the remove link is guarded by `{{#unless automatic}}`, but the `group-member` view (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6`) defines no `automatic` property/binding. In an itemView template this will not reliably resolve to the parent group’s `automatic` flag, so for automatic groups the condition can evaluate as “not automatic” (e.g., `automatic` undefined/falsey) and render the remove link. Clicking it calls `removeMember` -> `Group#removeMember` (DELETE `/admin/groups/:id/members.json`), and the backend explicitly returns 422 for automatic groups (`Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` / spec).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec uses xhr :put for remove_member but the route is delete; PUT routes to add_members which requires usernames param causing ActionController::ParameterMissing instead of expected 422
Route change removing get 'users' and changing response shape to {members:, meta:} envelope may break existing consumers expecting a bare array from old endpoints

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the `GroupsController#members` endpoint response from a bare serialized array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`) to an object envelope `{ members: ..., meta: ... }`, and the JS client is updated accordingly (`findMembers()` now expects `result.meta` and `result.members`). This is a backward-incompatible API shape change that could break any other (non-updated) consumers of `/groups/:group_id/members`, but the diff itself doesn’t show such external consumers, so it’s a compatibility concern rather than a verifiable functional defect within this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers empty-name early return now returns undefined instead of Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), causing .then() callers to throw
user-selector binding to controller 'usernames' property can desync after findMembers resets members, leaving stale input text and losing the previous persistence of membership via group save

adjudication.rationale: In the new flow, `usernames` is just a controller field (`usernames: null`) and is no longer derived from `members` (the old computed `usernames` based on `members.@each.username` was removed). `findMembers()` now updates `model.members` only, and `addMembers` explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not reset `this.usernames`, so the user-selector input can indeed remain stale after member list reloads. However, the claim that membership persistence is “lost via group save” is not a verifiable defect: the UI/API were redesigned so membership changes happen immediately via `addMembers`/`removeMember` endpoints, and `save()`/`create()` intentionally no longer send usernames (template also separates add-members with its own button).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination computeds (showingLast/currentPage/totalPages) depend on model properties via ObjectController proxying and can show stale values when the model is swapped without re-firing observers

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, pagination computeds are declared as `.property("limit", "offset", "user_count")` and `showingLast` compares `currentPage`/`totalPages`. Those keys live on the `Discourse.Group` model (`limit/offset/user_count` were added in `models/group.js`), and the controller relies on `Em.ObjectController` proxying to reach them. The computeds do not explicitly depend on `model`/`content` (e.g., `model.limit`), so if the controller’s `model` is swapped to a different group instance, it’s plausible these computeds won’t necessarily invalidate in sync with the content change unless the proxy emits change notifications for the proxied keys. This is a diff-grounded robustness concern, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it manifests as a broken UI in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking change to public /groups/:group_id/members response format from bare array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no spec coverage for the new format, pagination params, or old-format compatibility

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (bare array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` (object wrapper) in `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`, which is an API/contract change for `/groups/:group_id/members`. The client code is updated to consume `members` via `Group#findMembers` setting `members` on the model and templates iterating `{{#each m in members}}`, but there is no spec added/updated covering the new response shape or pagination params for the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint (only `Admin::GroupsController` specs are modified). Whether old-format compatibility is required isn’t shown, but the lack of coverage for this new contract is a concrete review issue grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, creating a phantom empty page
removeMember leaves UI on a blank page after deleting the last member of the last page because stale offset is clamped against old user_count and controller never adjusts offset/currentPage

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#removeMember`, after DELETE it calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. In `findMembers`, the requested `offset` is clamped using the *current* `user_count` (`Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`), which is stale (pre-delete). If you delete the last user on the last page, `offset` can remain past the new total (e.g. old total 51 -> offset 50, new total 50). The subsequent request `/groups/:name/members.json?offset=50` will return an empty `members` array (server uses the provided offset), and the model sets `members` to empty while `currentPage/totalPages` still indicates the last page, producing a blank members list. The controller has no logic to reduce `offset`/`currentPage` after `user_count` shrinks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips unknown usernames and returns success_json, with the spec covering that behavior deleted and not rewritten

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are split and each username is looked up; unknown usernames are simply ignored (only `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` then `group.add(user)`), and the action still proceeds to `group.save` and returns `success_json` on save (no validation/error for missing users). The prior spec coverage for silent success on non-existent usernames (in the removed PATCH incremental update tests) was deleted and no equivalent test was added for the new add_members endpoint, so this edge-case behavior is now untested.

The diff does not show the controller type/aliasing, so it’s not verifiable as a definite break, but it is a real, diff-grounded risk and there’s no added coverage for the public members rendering path.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same pagination boundary bug: when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, the logic allows an extra/phantom page (next offset becomes == user_count), resulting in an empty final page and confusing UX.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination offset is never clamped down, so findMembers reload after removal can strand the view on an offset past the end

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the offset is clamped with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`, which allows `offset === user_count` (and uses the pre-request `user_count` value) (group.js: `var ... offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));`). After `removeMember`, it simply calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. If you remove the only user on the last page, the stored `offset` can remain at the old last-page start, and the next request can be made with an offset that is now at/past the end, yielding an empty member list and leaving the view stranded on an invalid page until manually paged back.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group members route setupController sets model to a Discourse.Group but template iterates members which may not resolve, blanking the public group members page
Admin groups 'users' GET route removed with no replacement, causing 404s for existing clients

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the admin `get "users"` route under `resources :groups` (routes.rb), but member listing is replaced by a non-admin endpoint: `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now calls `/groups/:name/members.json` (GroupsController#members now returns `{members, meta}` with pagination). Admin UI code is updated to use `model.findMembers()` instead of the removed admin route. The claim that it was removed “with no replacement” is not supported by the diff; any impact to “existing clients” outside this codebase cannot be verified from the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public /groups/:name/members endpoint response shape changed from bare array to {members: [...], meta: {...}}, breaking existing consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, so the finding about a response-shape change is grounded. However, within this PR the in-repo consumer (`Discourse.Group#findMembers`) is also updated to call `/members.json` and to read `result.members`/`result.meta`, and the related routes/templates are adjusted, so nothing in the shown diff proves an in-app break. The remaining concern is API/backwards-compatibility for any other (possibly external) consumers of `/groups/:name/members` that aren’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers action never clears the usernames input after success, allowing accidental re-submission of same usernames
addMembers action gives no feedback on failure, e.g. non-existent usernames silently dropped server-side with no error

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and does not handle the returned promise or display any success/error state. On the server, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` splits `usernames` and only adds users that exist (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), silently ignoring unknown usernames and still returning `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. So the UI will give no indication that some requested usernames were ignored, but this is more a UX/API design gap than a verifiable functional defect (the endpoint is designed to succeed even with unknown usernames).

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips usernames that don't match a user and still returns success_json, leaving admins with no error for misspelled usernames

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; otherwise it does nothing and proceeds. It then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, regardless of whether any usernames were invalid/misspelled. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/feedback issue (no error/reporting for skipped usernames), but it’s not a clear correctness defect since the behavior is explicitly implemented and group.save can still legitimately succeed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed spec coverage for 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' leaves that behavior untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the spec `it "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"` from the old PATCH-based incremental membership update tests. The new implementation in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` still silently ignores unknown usernames (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), but there is no longer a test asserting this behavior for the new endpoint. This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage regression rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil, causing an off-by-one phantom empty page when user_count == limit

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., `user_count == limit`), this returns one extra page (e.g., `floor(1)+1 == 2` instead of 1). This would enable navigating to a “last” page that has no members, matching the off-by-one phantom page described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET /groups/:group_id/members response changed from bare JSON array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} without versioning, breaking existing API consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` (object wrapper with pagination meta). Internal JS callers were updated to use `result.members`/`result.meta` (e.g., `Discourse.Group#findMembers`), but the diff shows no backward-compat handling for clients expecting the old array shape. That’s a real, diff-grounded API compatibility concern, but it appears intentional to support pagination rather than an accidental correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PUT /admin/groups/:id silently drops membership update support (group[usernames] and PATCH add/delete path), ignoring usernames while returning success

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes membership updates from the group update endpoint: `Admin::GroupsController#update` no longer reads any `usernames` param (old `payload[:usernames]` path is gone), and the PATCH-specific `update_patch` (add/delete) logic is deleted entirely. The JS model similarly changes from `saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames` to plain `save/create`. Membership changes are now handled only via the new `/admin/groups/:group_id/members.json` PUT/DELETE endpoints (`add_members`/`remove_member`). So a client still sending `PUT/PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with usernames/changes would indeed be ignored while still returning success on save, but this appears to be an intentional API shift rather than an internal functional defect given the new endpoints and updated tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec uses xhr :put but routes.rb only wires the action as DELETE, so controller spec bypasses routing and a route/action mismatch ships undetected

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` under `context ".remove_member"`, the first example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but `config/routes.rb` wires `remove_member` as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Because this is a controller spec calling the action directly (not a routing/integration spec), the verb mismatch won’t be caught by routing and could allow a route/action mismatch to slip through. This is a test correctness/coverage issue rather than a production defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips nonexistent usernames and still renders success_json, surfacing no error for mistyped names

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are split and each is looked up with User.find_by_username; nonexistent usernames are simply skipped (no else branch) and the action still renders success_json as long as group.save succeeds. This matches the finding, but the diff doesn’t establish that this must be treated as an error (previous code also silently skipped missing users, and the removed spec even asserted silent success), so it’s more of a UX/behavior concern than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupController calls model.findMembers() without returning the promise, so loading machinery no longer waits and templates render before members exist; also findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise for empty name, breaking .then callers
remove_member has no guard that the user is actually a member, so removing a non-member returns success while membership is untouched

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code unconditionally does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. ActiveRecord association `delete` is a no-op if the user isn’t currently in the group, so the endpoint will still return success even though nothing changed. The diff doesn’t specify that this should error; this could be intentional idempotent behavior, but it is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/semantics concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.visible = params[:visible] == 'true' unconditionally flips the group to invisible when the param is omitted on partial updates

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the code sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally (no `if params[:visible].present?` guard). If an update request omits the `visible` param, `params[:visible]` is `nil`, the comparison evaluates to `false`, and the group will be saved as invisible. This behavior is directly implied by the new update implementation in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing PATCH update path breaks existing incremental-membership API: clients calling PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes now hit update, which ignores the payload and returns success_json with no membership change

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-specific membership update path: `update_patch` is deleted and `Admin::GroupsController#update` no longer branches on `request.patch?` or processes `params[:changes]` (add/delete usernames). Now `update` only updates `alias_level`, `visible`, and possibly `name`, then renders `success_json` on save. Therefore a client still sending `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes` will hit `update`, get a success response (assuming save passes), and no membership modifications will occur. The removed specs under the prior `context 'incremental'` further indicate this behavior was intentionally dropped without compatibility handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create action changed from params[:group][:name] to flat params[:name], so existing clients sending group: {name: ...} now get empty group name and validation errors

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#create, the payload handling was changed from nested params[:group][:name] (and params[:group][:visible]) to flat params[:name] / params[:visible] (see `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip`). There is no fallback to read `params[:group]`, so a client still POSTing `{ group: { name: ... } }` will result in `params[:name]` being nil, the name becoming an empty string, and `group.save` failing with validation errors. The diff confirms this breaking behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public /groups/:name/members response changed from serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} object without deprecation or versioning, breaking existing consumers

adjudication.rationale: `GroupsController#members` changes the response from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a top-level JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e. an object with `members` and `meta` keys. This is a breaking change to the public `/groups/:name/members(.json)` endpoint, and the diff shows no compatibility layer (e.g., optional param/versioning) or preservation of the previous array format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed ability to set group members at creation time (backend drops group.usernames; frontend createWithUsernames deleted), replacing one-step create-with-members with two-step flow and deleting its tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the one-step “create group with members” flow: frontend deletes `createWithUsernames` usage (admin-group.js now calls `group.create()`/`group.save()`), `Discourse.Group.asJSON()` no longer includes `usernames`, and `Admin::GroupsController#create` no longer accepts usernames (only `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]`). The admin template also only shows the add-members UI under `{{#if id}}`, forcing a two-step create-then-add flow. The previous create test asserting usernames were saved is removed/replaced. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change, but not inherently a correctness defect since member management is still possible via new `add_members` endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save() in admin-group.js.es6 discards membership edits in the usernames field, sending only name/alias_level/visible, giving a success toast with zero membership change

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, membership changes are no longer intended to be saved via the group’s save/create request. The old `usernames` computed property (derived from `members`) and `saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames` calls were removed. Instead, membership is managed explicitly via separate actions/endpoints: `addMembers` calls `model.addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` (PUT `/admin/groups/:id/members.json`) and `removeMember` calls `model.removeMember(member)` (DELETE `/admin/groups/:id/members.json`), both of which reload members. The template also labels the field as “Add members” and provides an Add button, not “edit all members then Save”. Therefore, `save()` not sending usernames is consistent with the new flow, not a discarded edit defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: user-selector in group.hbs still binds usernames but controller never initializes it from loaded members, leaving stale/empty state after deleting the usernames computed property and _usernames round-trip

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally changes semantics: `usernames` is no longer derived from the loaded `members` list for saving the whole membership. The old computed `usernames` (round-tripping `_usernames` based on `members.@each.username`) was removed, and group saving was changed from `saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames(this.get('usernames'))` to `group.save()` / `group.create()` (admin-group controller). Membership management is now done via separate `addMembers`/`removeMember` actions calling `Group#addMembers(usernames)` and `Group#removeMember(member)`, and the add-members `user-selector` in `group.hbs` is only for entering usernames to add, not mirroring current members. Therefore, not initializing `usernames` from `members` does not break the new behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded and unvalidated client-controlled `limit` on the public group members endpoint allows `limit=-1` (no limit) dumping entire group membership (user enumeration + DoS); needs clamping to a sane max

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is taken directly from `params[:limit]` and passed to ActiveRecord `.limit(limit)` with no validation/clamping: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` then `group.users...limit(limit)`. This allows client-controlled values like `-1` (which can behave as “no limit” in some DBs, e.g. Postgres `LIMIT -1`) or very large numbers, enabling full membership dumps / potential DoS via an unbounded query/response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `remove_member` in admin groups controller uses `group.users.delete(user_id)`, bypassing the model API (`group.remove`) and skipping before_destroy/counter-cache/audit logic, potentially leaving user_count and permission grants stale

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows membership removal is done via `group.users.delete(user_id)` (association delete) rather than the previously-used model API pattern (`group.remove(user)` existed in the removed `update_patch` code). That is a concrete change in behavior at the controller level and could bypass any encapsulated logic in `Group#remove` (callbacks, side-effects, bookkeeping), but the diff does not show what `group.remove` does or whether counter caches/audit/permission updates exist, so the claimed staleness is plausible but not verifiable as a definite defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `remove_member` operates on a client-supplied user_id with no check that the user is actually a member, and the unconditional success render masks silent no-op deletes

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the action takes `user_id` directly from params and calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` without verifying the user exists or is currently a member. If the user isn’t a member, `delete` is a no-op and the code still proceeds to `render json: success_json` as long as `group.save` returns truthy, so the API can report success even when nothing changed. Whether that’s a defect is debatable (DELETE can be treated as idempotent), but the diff does show the behavior described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#members new paginated response shape ({members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}) has zero specs; no test asserts meta keys, pagination windowing, or total correctness

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members, GroupUserSerializer)` to a new JSON envelope with `members:` and `meta: { total, limit, offset }` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb). In the provided diff, the only spec changes are in `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, and there are no added/updated specs covering `GroupsController#members` or asserting the new `meta` keys/pagination semantics. While the diff can’t prove there are zero specs elsewhere in the repo, it does show this new nontrivial response shape/pagination logic was introduced without accompanying tests in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::GroupsController non-automatic update happy path untested; old test covering name change and membership via PUT was deleted, so regressions in name assignment or alias_level persistence pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#update semantics (now reads params[:alias_level], params[:visible], params[:name] directly and allows renaming when !group.automatic), but the spec no longer covers the non-automatic update happy path. In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb, the previous PUT update test that asserted name change and membership update was removed, and the remaining ".update" coverage only checks that automatic groups ignore name changes. There is no test asserting that a regular group can be renamed and/or that alias_level changes persist, so regressions in these update fields could slip through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent-skip branch for nonexistent usernames in add_members had its specs deleted without replacement; only valid users tested, so behavior of silently dropping unknown usernames is unpinned

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, nonexistent usernames are still silently ignored (`usernames.split(",").each` then `if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end` with no else/error). The previous spec that pinned this behavior (`it "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"` in the removed incremental PATCH update tests) was deleted, and the new `context ".add_members"` only tests adding valid users / automatic-group rejection, leaving the silent-skip behavior untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::GroupsController create error path (render_json_error) untested; no spec posts invalid input like blank name

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#create` now has an explicit failure branch: `if group.save ... else render_json_error group` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb). The updated specs add a `.create` test only for stripping spaces (`xhr :post, :create, name: " bob "`) but do not exercise invalid input (e.g., blank/whitespace-only name => `group.name` becomes `""`) to verify the `render_json_error` path. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly changed controller behavior, not a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Automatic-group tests hardcode group_id: 1 instead of fabricating groups, breaking under seed-id changes and silently testing seed data rather than the automatic guard logic

adjudication.rationale: The spec additions do hardcode `group_id: 1` / `id: 1` for “automatic group” behavior instead of fabricating an automatic group in the test. Examples in the diff: `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, ...` ("ignore name change on automatic group"), `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...` ("cannot add members to automatic groups"), and `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, ...`. This makes the tests depend on a particular seeded automatic group existing with ID 1, which is fragile and can silently test seed configuration rather than the guard logic if IDs/seed data change. It’s a test-quality issue, not a production defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent data loss for existing clients: new update controller only reads flat params and ignores params[:group][:usernames], so old-payload membership edits are silently discarded with a success 200 response

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff changes from reading `payload = params[:group]` (and applying `payload[:usernames]` to modify membership) to reading only flat params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) and never processing `params[:group][:usernames]` or any membership changes. If an existing client still sends the old payload shape (`group[usernames]=...`) to `PUT /admin/groups/:id`, the controller will ignore it, `group.save` will likely succeed, and it will return `success_json` (200), silently dropping the intended membership update. Membership updates were moved to new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints, but the old update behavior is not rejected or handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Expand+contract violation: old PATCH update path and get "users" route removed in same change as replacement endpoints, causing PATCH requests with changes: {add/delete} to be silently ignored during rolling deploys

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the old incremental membership update path (`update_patch` handling `params[:changes][:add|:delete]`) and the controller `update` action no longer checks `request.patch?` or processes `params[:changes]`. Since Rails `resources :groups` will still route PATCH to `update`, a legacy client sending `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: {add/delete}` will hit the new `update`, ignore the membership changes, and likely return success if the group saves—i.e., the request is silently ignored. Separately, the admin route `get "users"` under `resources :groups` is removed and replaced with `PUT/DELETE members`, which is also a breaking change during rolling deploys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops unknown usernames and returns success with no log or error result

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are split and each is looked up via User.find_by_username; unknown usernames are simply skipped (no else branch), and the action still renders success_json if group.save succeeds. This means callers can get a success response even if some/all usernames were invalid, with no indication of which were added vs ignored. This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/UX/API design concern, but not an outright verifiable defect since silent ignore of unknown users may be intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member reports success for a no-op when user_id isn't a member or join row already deleted

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is intentionally idempotent: if the join row doesn’t exist (user not a member / already deleted), it’s a no-op and the action will still render `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds. The prior implementation explicitly tested/allowed silent success for removing non-members (see removed spec `it "succeeds silently when removing non-members"` in the diff), so “reports success for a no-op” is not a verifiable defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers mutates offset optimistically before the request resolves with no rollback on failure

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `next`/`previous` actions set `group.offset` immediately (`group.set("offset", offset);`) before calling `group.findMembers()`. `findMembers` only re-syncs `offset` inside the `.then(...)` success path (sets `offset: result.meta.offset`), and there is no `.catch`/failure handling to revert the optimistic `offset` update. If the AJAX call fails, the model remains with the new offset while `members` stays stale, causing inconsistent pagination state (e.g., `currentPage` changes based on `offset` even though the member list didn’t load).

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers has no concurrency guard, so double-clicking next fires overlapping requests and out-of-order responses overwrite newer state (last-response-wins)

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` that unconditionally `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` on the model based on the response (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js). The admin controller actions `next`/`previous` update `group.offset` and then call `group.findMembers()` (admin-group.js.es6). There is no request sequencing/cancellation/guard, so rapid repeated clicks can trigger overlapping requests where an older request resolves after a newer one and overwrites `members`/`offset` with stale data (the response also sets `offset` from `result.meta.offset`). This is a verifiable last-response-wins race introduced/exposed by the new pagination/stateful `findMembers` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route setupController in admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6 calls findMembers() without returning the promise, rendering an empty list immediately and leaving request rejection unhandled
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that findMembers() is asynchronous but its promise is not handled/returned, so the controller renders before member data arrives (race condition/empty list) and failures may go unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers never clears the input and has no success/failure feedback or in-flight guard on the button

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and only calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without resetting `usernames`, so the input will remain populated after submission. In `admin/templates/group.hbs`, the "Add" button (`<button {{action "addMembers"}} ...>`) has no `disabled`/in-flight binding and there is no success/failure UI handling in the action (no `.then/.catch`), so repeated clicks can trigger multiple requests and the user gets no feedback. This is a UX/completeness concern rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group members endpoint has no cap on the limit parameter, allowing unbounded membership serialization in one response

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is taken directly from `params[:limit]` (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`) and then applied to the query (`.limit(limit)`) and serialization without any upper bound. A client can request an arbitrarily large `limit`, causing unbounded membership rows to be loaded/serialized in one response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined when name is empty, breaking the always-promise contract and risking errors with future .then chaining

adjudication.rationale: In Discourse.Group#findMembers the guard clause was changed from returning a resolved promise (`Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`) to returning `undefined` when `name` is empty: `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`. This does break the prior “always returns a thenable” behavior and would throw if any caller does `group.findMembers().then(...)`. In this diff, the existing `.then` usages in routes were removed and current call sites just invoke `findMembers()` without chaining, so it’s not a directly verifiable runtime break here, but it is a real API/contract regression that can cause errors for future or external callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member relies on group.save persisting a join-row deletion; validation failure blocks the deletion and leaves the in-memory users association mutated after a failed response

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the join-row deletion is executed by `group.users.delete(user_id)` before `group.save` is called. In Rails, `association.delete` removes the join record immediately; it does not depend on `group.save` to persist that deletion. Therefore a validation failure on `group.save` would not “block the deletion” as claimed (it could at most cause an error response after the deletion already happened).
